Welcome to Greenleaf
At Greenleaf School, we are proud to provide an inspirational, inclusive, and high-quality education within a vibrant and engaging environment. Our aim is simple: to nurture self-confident, respectful pupils who take pride in themselves, their school, and the wider community.
Our motto—Aim High, Work Hard, Be Kind—guides everything we do. It shapes our learning, our relationships, and the way we support every child to reach their full potential.
Located in the heart of Walthamstow, Greenleaf is a place where children and staff flourish together. We celebrate our achievements and value the strong partnerships we build with our pupils, families, staff, and the wider community.
We look forward to welcoming you to our school.

Vision and Values
Our Vision
At Greenleaf Primary School, our community is a thriving tree - rooted in respect, nourished by kindness, and reaching ever upward through aspiration. Our school is safe and inclusive; rights are respected; differences are welcomed and diversity is our strength.
Through our shared values of Respect, Growth Mindset, Kindness, Belonging, and Aspiration, we guide our children to become thoughtful, confident, and resilient learners. We believe that with care, encouragement, and high expectations, every child can achieve more than they ever thought possible.
Together, with our community, we cultivate joy in learning, celebrate diversity, and nurture strong roots of respect and fairness so that all our children leave Greenleaf continuing to aim high, work hard and be kind.
Greenleaf Values
To bring our values to life, each of our house teams will be promoting a school value. This will help children develop a deeper understanding of what our values look like in action, both in the classroom and beyond, and strengthen our sense of community and shared purpose.
We care for ourselves, others, and our world.
We keep trying, learn from mistakes, and never give up.
We are gentle, fair, and help others feel happy and safe.
We include everyone and know we are stronger together.
We dream big, work hard, and believe we can achieve anything.
Belonging Art Mural in collaboration with Angry Dan
We have been delighted to work alongside street artist Angry Dan on our exciting collaborative mural project that brings our school value of Belonging to life.
Throughout the project, children have shared their ideas, experiences and creativity, helping to shape a vibrant piece of artwork that reflects the diversity, unity and spirit of our school community. The mural celebrates the importance of every child feeling seen, valued and connected, creating a lasting visual reminder that everyone belongs here.
We are incredibly proud of what our pupils have achieved and grateful to Angry Dan for inspiring and guiding them throughout this creative journey.

Welcome to Greenleaf
Primary School
It is my great pleasure to welcome you to Greenleaf Primary School.
At Greenleaf, we want every child to feel happy, valued and inspired to achieve their very best. Our motto, Aim High, Work Hard, Be Kind, is at the heart of everything we do and reflects both our ambition for every child and the values that guide our school community.
At Greenleaf, children are encouraged to aim high, discover what they love and grow in confidence. We offer a rich and exciting curriculum, exceptional opportunities for outdoor play and a caring, inclusive environment where every child is known and valued.
A School Where Children Flourish
Situated in the heart of Walthamstow, Greenleaf is a warm, inclusive and ambitious school where children and adults flourish together.
From their first days in Reception to the end of Year 6, we support every child to grow in confidence, discover their strengths and develop a genuine love of learning. We want our pupils to leave us as confident, capable and compassionate young people, ready for their next steps.
Learning Inside and Beyond the Classroom
We provide a broad, engaging curriculum that builds strong foundations in Reading, Writing and Maths while giving children opportunities to explore their interests, develop new skills and discover the wider world.
Learning extends well beyond the classroom through educational visits, projects, extracurricular activities and a wide range of clubs. From sport and drama to languages, arts and crafts, there are opportunities for every child to try something new, develop their talents and have fun.
As an accredited International School, we encourage our children to celebrate diversity, explore different cultures and develop an understanding of the wider world. We want them to become curious, confident and responsible global citizens.
The Power of Play
Play is an important part of childhood and a valued part of life at Greenleaf.
Through our commitment to OPAL (Outdoor Play and Learning), children have rich opportunities to develop creativity, teamwork, resilience and independence through imaginative, high-quality outdoor play.
In May 2026, we were incredibly proud to receive the OPAL Platinum Award, the highest level of recognition for outstanding play provision. This is a fantastic achievement and reflects the commitment of our whole school community to giving children the very best opportunities to play, explore and learn.
Caring, Ambitious and Inclusive
Our dedicated staff combine high expectations with excellent pastoral care. We know that children learn best when they feel safe, supported and valued, and we work hard to ensure every child feels a strong sense of belonging.
Strong relationships are at the heart of our school. By working closely with pupils, families and our wider community, we create an environment where everyone is encouraged to succeed and thrive.
We also provide high-quality wraparound care, led and delivered by our own school staff. Our breakfast and after-school provision gives families a safe, welcoming and familiar environment for their children before and after the school day.
Come and See Greenleaf for Yourself
I hope our website gives you a glimpse of what makes Greenleaf such a special place to learn, grow and belong.
If you would like to find out more, please get in touch. We would be delighted to welcome you to Greenleaf and show you our school in action.

At Greenleaf, we see the personal development of our pupils as an integral part of curriculum offer.

Greenleaf Breakfast and After School Clubs
Breakfast Club 7:45-8:45am
After School Club 3:20-6:00pm
Our term time wraparound care provision is designed to support families who require childcare beyond the standard school day, while providing children with a safe, welcoming, and enriching environment. We operate these during term time.
Our Breakfast Club runs from 7:45am to 8:45am, offering children a healthy and nutritious breakfast to start their day. Alongside this, pupils can take part in a variety of calm and engaging activities, helping them settle into the school day in a positive and relaxed way.
Our After School Club operates from 3:20pm to 6:00pm, providing a balance of physical play and more focused activities. This ensures children can unwind, socialise, and continue developing their interests in a supportive setting.
Wraparound Care is led by our dedicated school staff, creating a familiar, safe, and nurturing environment for all pupils. Being based on the school site allows for a smooth and seamless transition between the school day and childcare provision, giving children a strong sense of continuity and security.
For our younger pupils in Nursery, Reception, and Year 1, staff personally escort children to their classrooms after Breakfast Club and collect them at the end of the school day for After School Club. Older pupils are supported to make their own way to and from sessions, encouraging independence within a safe structure.
Whether children need an early start to the day or extended care in the afternoon, our Wraparound provision offers a supportive environment where wellbeing is prioritised, and children can learn, play, and thrive.
Our current costs are:
Breakfast Club is £5.50
After School Club is £12.50
Breakfast club is open every day from 7.45am until 8.45am during term time. Children are provided with healthy breakfast options and offered a choice of indoor activities. We offer low sugar cereals, toast including wholegrain varieties, low fat spreads, fresh fruit, water and milk. . During the session children have a range of indoor and outdoor activities to participate in. We ask the children for their ideas and incorporate these during the week.
After School Club Snacks
After School Club is from 3:20pm to 6:00pm during term time. Children are asked to bring a small snack from home. Water is available for children to refill their bottles at school.
To support our healthy school approach, we would like to remind everyone of our snack expectations for After School Club. To ensure consistency across the day, we ask that snacks brought from home reflect the same healthy standards we set during school hours
Here are some healthy snack suggestions:
To keep our standards consistent, please do not send the following:
If any food items needs to be kept chilled then you can pass it to the Breakfast Club staff in the morning. Please label the container with your child's name.
Sandwich or bagel
Crackers or breadsticks
Crisps, biscuits, chocolate or other sweet treats.
No nuts or nut-containing products
Apply for a Place
If you require more information or would like to enquire about places, please contact the school office. If you wish to apply for a place, please complete the Booking Form below and return it to: bcandasc@greenleaf.waltham.sch.uk
The school will then contact you in due course about availability.

Extra- Curricular Clubs and Activities
At our school, we are proud to offer a wide range of exciting clubs and extra-curricular activities designed to spark curiosity, develop new skills, and foster a sense of community among our students. From creative arts to sports and critical thinking, there is something for every student to explore and enjoy.
Our clubs are designed to inspire and engage, helping students to pursue their passions and discover new interests outside of the classroom. Whether your child loves to create, compete, or connect with others, they will find a club that suits their interests and encourages personal growth.
If your child is not enrolled in a club but would like to join one, please contact the school office team to see if there are any spaces: school@greenleaf.waltham.sch.uk
Music Tuition
In addition, we also offer music tuition. Spaces for these clubs available at the start of the academic year for parents to sign up. Our current music tuition is piano, violin, clarinet, flute and orchestra.
Choice of Clubs
We have a wide range of clubs on offer ranging from sports, crafts and languages. Each term, parents are given the opportunity to sign up to the different clubs. Some are led by Greenleaf staff and some are led by external organisers.

Partnerships for Inclusion of Neurodiversity in Schools (PINS)
Greenleaf Primary School is part of the Partnership for Inclusion of Neurodiversity in Schools (PINS). This is a national funded programme which aims to improve outcomes for children and young people attending mainstream primary schools who are neurodiverse. The approach of PINS has been developed around the key principles of Autism in Schools which are:
The PINS project is funded by the Department for Education (DfE), supported by the Department for Health and Social Care (DHSC) and NHS England (NHSE). Greenleaf Primary School is working with advisory teachers as well as other key professionals as part of the PINS project too.
A whole school approach
Good quality training for staff
Supporting parents groups
Understanding students' experience of schools.
How we will be working with PINS
Through our involvement in the PINS project, we will be:
Greenleaf Primary School has been involved with a range of professionals through this partnership, including speech and language therapists and occupational therapists, as well as undertaking other specialised training.
The goal of the PINS programme is to leave a sustainable impact, building a legacy of closer collaboration between schools, parents/carers, education and health. This will reframe the focus of specialist input to how a supportive learning environment and well-equipped school can improve the outcomes for neurodiverse children. This will in turn foster the development of whole-school approaches to support neurodiverse pupils.
We are proud to be part of the PINS project and look forward to working in partnership with our families to create the best possible outcomes for our pupils. Further updates will be shared as the project develops.
For more information from the DFE regarding the PINS project then click here.

Pupil Voice and Leadership
Article 12 in The United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child states that, ‘Every child has the right to express their views, feelings and wishes in all matters affecting them, and to have their views considered and taken seriously’ (UNICEF)
At Greenleaf Primary School, we value every child’s voice and ensure pupils have regular opportunities to share their ideas and opinions. Through methods such as School Council, surveys, learning walks and suggestion boxes, children actively contribute to school improvement and see how their input leads to real change.
We also promote strong pupil leadership, giving children meaningful roles and responsibilities that help develop their communication, organisation and confidence. Through these opportunities, pupils grow into articulate, responsible leaders, prepared for future challenges and real-life situations.
Here are the following roles we have in our school:

Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) and Inclusion
At Greenleaf Primary School, every child matters—and we expect the very best from everyone in our community. Working in close partnership with parents, we ensure all pupils have equal access to a rich, broad and balanced curriculum that meets their individual needs and prepares them for the future.
We celebrate every child as an individual, supporting them to grow at the right pace with the right level of challenge and care. Our curriculum is thoughtfully designed so that all pupils—including those with SEND—can thrive, succeed and take part fully in enriching experiences both in school and beyond.
Inclusion is at the heart of everything we do. Our skilled staff deliver high-quality teaching, underpinned by strong subject knowledge and carefully adapted to meet the needs of every learner. Where additional support is needed, targeted interventions and personalised provision ensure every child is given the opportunity to achieve their full potential

Greenleaf Primary School Governing Body
School governors are people who want to make a positive contribution to children’s education. Governors are one of the largest volunteer forces in the country and have an important part to play in raising school standards. The role of the governing body is absolutely key to the effectiveness of a school.
Our Governors ensure that our school provides a positive educational experience for all in our school community. They are committed to ensuring that all of our children get the best possible start in life. Governors at Greenleaf monitor the leadership of our school with regards to curriculum, standards and financial management, as well as the safeguarding of our pupils.
Each individual governor is a member of a governing body, which is established in law as a corporate body. Individual governors may not act independently of the rest of the governing body; decisions are the joint responsibility of the governing body. The role of the governing body is a strategic one, its key functions are to:
Please click here for our Governors' Annual Statement.
holding the Head Teacher to account
overseeing the financial performance of the school

The Structure of our Governing Board
Governors are part of the largest volunteer workforce in the country; they play a key role in helping the school provide the best possible education for all its pupils.
The structure of our Governing Board is as follows:
Once appointed Governors serve a four-year term of office.
Governors visit the school regularly so that they kept are informed of all aspects of school life. Each Governor is also linked to a subject area a.
Every year Governors self-evaluate their skills and experiences which contribute to Greenleaf having an effective Governing Body. Where gaps are identified, governors consider whether any particular action (eg. training) needs to be put in place.
The Headteacher and Governing Body work in close partnership. The Headteacher discusses all the main aspects of school life with the governing body and expects the governing body to both challenge and support the school. Acting as a “critical friend”, the governing body offers support and constructive advice; governors question proposals and seek further information to enable them to make sound decisions.

Tours for New Parents
Welcome to Greenleaf Primary School, we are pleased that you are considering applying for a Reception place for your child. Starting school is an exciting time for children and here at Greenleaf we want to ensure that you have all the information you need to make an informed choice.
Come and See Our School in Action
We would love to welcome prospective parents to one of our Open Mornings and give you a chance to experience our school for yourself.
The morning will begin at 9:30am with a warm welcome and presentation from our Headteacher, followed by a tour of the school. You’ll have the opportunity to see our pupils learning and get a real feel for the welcoming, happy atmosphere that makes our school special.
The visit will last no longer than 90 minutes, with plenty of opportunity to ask questions along the way.
We look forward to welcoming you and showing you what makes our school such a wonderful place to learn and grow.
Book a Reception Open Morning Place
To book your place, please click the date and complete the Google Form.
*New date added* Monday 7th December at 9:30am
If none of the Open Morning dates are convenient for you, please contact the school office to arrange a school visit.
Wednesday 18th November at 9:30am -Fully Booked
In-Year Admissions for Reception to Year 6
We welcome applications for children seeking a place in Reception through to Year 6 where places are available. Whether your family has recently moved into the area, your child is transferring from another school, or your circumstances have changed, we would be very happy to hear from you.
If you are interested in applying for an in-year place, please apply through Waltham Forest Admissions.
We would encourage you to get in touch with us if you have any questions about joining Greenleaf. We would be delighted to tell you more about our school, our values and what life is like here. Please get in touch with the school office to arrange a school visit.
Please contact the school office: school@greenleaf.waltham.sch.uk

Global Learning at Greenleaf
At Greenleaf, we hold international activities at the core of everything we do. We pride ourselves on being a multi-cultural school where we celebrate diversity. Our curriculum embeds a global approach throughout the school and our children are challenged to think carefully about the planet that they will inhabit. This is made possible by having a team who are motivated to ensure that the children have an enriching experience which empowers them to be global citizens, ready for the future.
We follow the seventeen Sustainable Development Goals which guide everything we do. Here are just a few ways in which we embed the goals into our curriculum:
Nursery learn about caring for animals and their environment (Goal 15 - Life on Land).
In Reception, one of the themes studied is Interdependence and understanding how families, people, animals and the environment all rely on one another. (Goal 17- Partnerships for the Goals).
Year 1 look at the lives of the Windrush Generation in Walthamstow and think about how we can ensure that we develop our skills in tackling racism and inequality (Goal 10 - Reduced Inequalities).
Year 2 explore healthy living (inside and out) and the basic needs of all animals and plants to survive (Goal 3- Good Health and Well Being).
Year 3 study the text Iron Man which warns of the dangers of our overconsumption on the planet (Goal 12- Responsible Consumption and Production).
In Year 4, one of the topics is Water and Ice which looks at our water usage and how we rely on it to ensure we survive (Goal 6 -Clean Water and Sanitation).
Year 5 read Journey to Jo’Burg, a text which explores racism and its links to poverty in South Africa during Apartheid. Focusing on how we can ensure access to opportunity is available to all, not just those with money or of a certain race/background (Goal 1 –No Poverty).
Year 6 take a trip to the Royal Courts of Justice as part of their Crime and Punishment topic (Goal 16 -Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions) and think about how important it is that rule of law is upheld in society.
Those interested in learning more about global learning can find out more at these sites:
https://globaldimension.org.uk
https://www.globalgoals.org
If you have any skills or global sessions you would like to deliver, or even if you would just like to find out more, then please email the school office.
